title: Pauser can sandwich pause/unpause cycles to selectively deny yield to specific stakers
description: The pauser role has unilateral pause/unpause power with no minimum unpause-cooldown and no commit-reveal on the timing. A pauser observing a substantial accStablePerShare credit pending after collectReward can pause immediately after the credit and force liquidity-constrained users into pauseWithdraw, which silently forfeits the pending rewards. The forfeited share is then implicitly redistributed to the pauser-aligned cohort on unpause.
impact: Pauser-aligned stakers extract a disproportionate yield share; targeted stakers forced into pauseWithdraw forfeit accrued rewards. This sharpens the documented KI-6 pauser trust assumption into a concrete economic exploitation pattern. Dual-listed as L-05 to ensure the operational/observability angle reaches the QA bundle as well.
attackPath: Pauser observes a substantial accStablePerShare credit pending after collectReward.
Pauser pauses immediately after the credit.
Target user, needing liquidity, calls pauseWithdraw — forfeiting rewards.
Pauser unpauses; pauser-aligned stakers claim normally.
likelihood: depends on pauser acting adversarially or colluding
assumptions: Adversarial / colluding pauser; KI-6 acknowledges pauser trust
recommendation: Add (a) a minimum unpause-cooldown so pause cannot be re-armed for a configurable window after every unpause, (b) require the pauser to be a multisig or DAO module rather than an EOA, and (c) emit Paused/Unpaused events with sufficient context for off-chain monitoring. Pairs naturally with the M-01 / L-05 pauseWithdraw rebase recommendation.
classifierRationale: Root cause IS KI-6 pauser trust. Routes to C bundle as sanitizer predicted.
